examples.title: First close: earned revenue is different from billings and cash
examples.review: Three job-cost source groups totaling 270,000 tie to J01–J03; the cash receipts and disbursements tie to J06–J08. All evidence IDs are unique.

examples.title: Second close: modification and revised cost estimate
examples.calculation: 500,000 / 1,000,000 = 50%; cumulative revenue = 650,000; current revenue = 650,000 − 360,000 = 290,000. Cumulative profit = 150,000; current profit = 60,000. Billings exceed revenue by 10,000; present a contract liability for this contract. AR = 660,000 − 550,000 = 110,000. Cash = 130,000 + 310,000 − 240,000 = 200,000.
examples.review: The revised estimate is not overwritten into the July workpaper. J12 records only the incremental earned revenue. J17 reclassifies the single-contract credit balance; other contracts are not netted.

examples.title: Separate branch: major uninstalled purchased equipment
conditions: One performance obligation; the purchased pumps are not distinct.
Customer control of the pumps transfers significantly before installation; the pump cost is significant.
Pumps are bought from a third party, with no significant contractor design/manufacturing involvement, and the contractor is principal. All ASC 606-10-55-21(b) conditions are assumed satisfied.
examples.review: This exception is not a blanket rule that every stored material is recorded at zero margin. Its conditions must be evidenced.

examples.title: Separate branch: full anticipated loss without double counting
conditions: The customer-specification construction contract is within ASC 605-35; contract-level loss policy applies.
No variable consideration, credit-risk adjustment or other contract asset impairment changes the isolated loss calculation.

Fixed consideration only, no credit-risk adjustment or capitalized contract-cost asset, one loss-assessment unit. ASC 605-35-25-46A does not apply the ASC 606 revenue constraint when measuring expected consideration for the loss test; do not mechanically reuse a constrained claim amount.
examples.calculation: Progress = 580,000 / 1,450,000 = 40%; revenue = 520,000. Normal cumulative loss = 60,000. Entire expected loss = 150,000. Additional provision = 150,000 − 60,000 = 90,000; debit contract cost and credit loss provision 90,000.
examples.review: Accruing an additional 150,000 would double count the 60,000 loss already recognized. The scope must be assessed separately from over-time revenue.

examples.title: Conditional retainage inside the first-close contract asset
conditions: The 30,000 retention is payable only after a substantive remaining performance condition; it is excluded from the 300,000 unconditional billings.
examples.calculation: 30,000 conditional retention + 30,000 other unbilled earned consideration = 60,000 contract asset. The separate unconditional AR remains 60,000.
examples.review: If only passage of time remains before payment, classification changes to receivable; the label retainage alone does not decide it.

examples.title: A disputed additional claim is not silently added to price
conditions: For this branch only, enforceable entitlement and the variable-consideration constraint are not yet supported. No legal conclusion is assumed.
examples.calculation: Price retained in this workpaper = 1,300,000; disputed amount tracked separately = 150,000; recognized increment from the disputed claim = 0.
examples.review: Unsigned does not automatically mean unapproved: contracts can be oral or implied. Preserve the correspondence and separate enforceability, modification approval, measurement and constraint conclusions.

examples.title: Reopened job with a late invoice
examples.calculation: Potential omitted cost population = 15,000; no automatic journal or revenue catch-up is prescribed until error-versus-estimate and cutoff facts are established.
examples.review: Retain the original close, invoice service dates, prior available information, estimate approval and discovery timestamp. Determine whether facts indicate an error, new estimate information or already accrued liability; avoid duplicate cost on reopening.

examples.title: Estimate-only revision, without new work or billing
examples.origin: Original synthetic alternative to July base, not additive to other branches
examples.review: New estimate information is assumed, not correction of known prior facts. Period remeasurement follows ASC 606-10-25-35; a negative catch-up is possible without a loss-making contract.

examples.title: Reopened July workpaper: approved credit and omitted July service
examples.origin: Original synthetic alternative management workpaper; base history retained
conditions: July service was incurred, recoverable performance cost, not previously accrued; 5,000 credit corrects the earlier quantity.
900,000 total expected cost already included this work and remains approved; no new contract price or cash/billing event.
These facts illustrate a corrected workpaper. ASC 250 materiality, issuance dates, prior-period error treatment and disclosures require separate review.
examples.review: If the 15,000 was already accrued, invoice arrival reclassifies the accrual to AP and adds zero cost/revenue. If it is a new September service, leave July untouched. Carry corrected cumulative balances forward before recomputing August; never add this branch to the original August close unchanged.

examples.title: Conditional retainage offsets the same contract liability
examples.origin: Original synthetic standalone branch, not an alteration of base unconditional billing assumptions
examples.calculation: AR = 690,000 - 550,000 = 140,000. Net contract liability = 690,000 - 650,000 = 40,000, also 70,000 advance less 30,000 conditional retainage.
examples.review: Conditional retainage is part of the one net contract position, not a second asset against a gross 70,000 liability. Do not offset a different contract or separate unconditional AR. FASB staff paper paragraphs 5-7 and 12.

examples.title: Stored material without customer control
examples.origin: Original synthetic counterexample to the uninstalled-goods branch
examples.review: Storage location, payment certification or an invoice alone does not establish customer control. Test control before any no-margin revenue; evaluate inventory/cost-asset treatment separately. No full alternate revenue calculation without an approved remaining-performance estimate.

evidence_controls.question: Is the job-cost population complete?
evidence_controls.procedure: Reconcile payroll batches, vendor invoice totals, goods receipts and accruals to the job ledger and GL. A matching total alone cannot reveal equal-and-opposite omissions; retain record counts and identifiers.
evidence_controls.failure: Unrecorded subcontract invoice, wrong job, duplicate invoice, unmatched credit note or excluded payroll batch.

evidence_controls.question: Can revisions and deletions be reconstructed?
evidence_controls.procedure: Keep source ID, version, effective period, received timestamp, superseded value, deletion marker and approval. A corrected invoice replaces its prior version in the active population and retains the audit trail.
evidence_controls.failure: Treating a tombstone as a zero-value new invoice leaves the old cost active; summing every version double counts.

evidence_controls.question: Does the close reconcile beyond WIP?
evidence_controls.procedure: Tie current revenue to cumulative minus prior recognized revenue; reconcile bills to AR, AR to cash receipts, payroll/AP to payments, and equity plus liabilities to assets.
evidence_controls.failure: Using billings as revenue conceals contract assets/liabilities and destroys the performance-to-cash bridge.

evidence_controls.question: What is the authority boundary?
evidence_controls.procedure: This record contains illustrative journals and reviewer questions. It provides no accounting-system connection or execution permission.
evidence_controls.failure: A numerically balanced entry can still have the wrong period, scope, legal basis or cost population.

title: US management accounting: shared-service allocation and budget-to-actual bridge
summary: Original synthetic US manufacturer case with a reconciled shared-service allocation, independent headcount sensitivity, sequential volume-price bridge, versioned forecast and restated actual, margin definitions, and profit-to-cash reconciliation.
jurisdiction: United States; synthetic privately held domestic manufacturer

provenance.reviewer: Codex AI-assisted original-source and synthetic-fixture review
provenance.note: Original synthetic fixture and bounded source synthesis for AA-I125. No customer data, operating records, professional sign-off, or source full text is included.

rights.external_content: External text is not included; publisher terms apply.

data.title: US management accounting: shared-service allocation and budget-to-actual bridge
data.summary: One synthetic US manufacturer, one January 2026 reporting population, and independent allocation and planning branches.
data.accountable_owner: Controller or FP&A owner; a financial-reporting or federal-award specialist reviews any external branch.
data.scope: A privately held domestic US manufacturer using US GAAP for the external ledger and a documented internal management policy for January 2026. The federal-award and federal-contract branches are counterexamples requiring separate authority.
frameworks: 2 CFR Part 200 only when a federal-award branch applies
FAR Part 31 only when a covered federal-contract branch applies
inputs: external award or contract terms if applicable
assumptions: All amounts are USD and project-created.
January 2026 is a closed monthly management period; the budget was approved 2025-12-15.
The support pool contains only support payroll, benefits, and software/occupancy; direct production payroll and restructuring costs are excluded.
The primary driver is approved support-service hours because the synthetic service records describe support consumption; this is a documented management choice, not an economic finding.
The entity-level profit-to-cash bridge has no noncash items in the fixture; the zero is an explicit assumption, not a plug.
The budget-to-actual revenue bridge uses a sequential volume-then-price convention; no mix or efficiency effect is included in the two-factor population.

events.event: January activity and support pool incurred
Forecast v2 revised using known January actuals
Late $1,000 direct-cost invoice received for January
January actual v2 restated; v1 is retained and not added

excluded_costs.label: direct production payroll
excluded_costs.reason: Charged to the direct production cost object; not in the shared pool.

excluded_costs.label: one-time restructuring
excluded_costs.reason: Reported separately from recurring management margin; not in the pool.

cost_pool.ledger_reconciliation: 90000 + 20000 + 10000 = 120000; excluded costs are not used as a plug.

sensitivity.interpretation: Sensitivity only. It does not prove that headcount or hours is the correct economic driver.

allocation.rationale: Approved support-service hours are used for the primary internal view because the synthetic service log describes resource consumption. The controller must document the rationale, approve changes, and preserve the headcount branch as a separate sensitivity.
allocation.external_boundary: A federal-award or covered federal-contract charge requires separate applicability, consistent direct-versus-indirect treatment, benefit analysis, documentation, award or contract terms, and possible CAS review. Internal reconciliation alone is insufficient.

actual_v2_restatement.reason: A $1,000 January direct-cost invoice was received on 2026-02-09 and added to AP.
actual_v2_restatement.restatement_rule: Replace v1 for the restated view; do not add v1 and v2 together.

invalid_alternative.name: price at budget volume
invalid_alternative.reason: It uses a different convention and cannot be added to the sequential price effect without double counting.

unit_a_operating_margin.numerator: Unit A revenue - Unit A direct cost - Unit A allocated support
unit_a_operating_margin.label: Internal management view, not a GAAP measure

entity_operating_profit.numerator: entity revenue - entity direct cost - full support pool
entity_operating_profit.denominator: not a margin in this bridge
entity_operating_profit.label: Synthetic entity reconciliation, not an external reporting conclusion

contribution_margin.reason: The fixture does not provide a validated variable-cost taxonomy beyond direct production cost.

profit_bridge.no_double_counting_rule: The entity profit uses the full $120,000 pool once. Unit A's $72,000 allocation is a management view and is not added to entity profit.

cash_bridge.interpretation: The late invoice changes profit and AP but not cash closing balance because it remains unpaid. Zero noncash items are an explicit fixture assumption.

counterexamples.scenario: The same $120,000 pool is proposed for a federal award using the 30/70 headcount sensitivity because it produces a preferred result.
counterexamples.reason: The internal sensitivity does not establish relative benefit, consistent treatment, documentation, award-term compliance, or CAS/FAR applicability. Apply 2 CFR §§200.403 and 200.405 and any applicable contract or award terms before charging the award.

counterexamples.scenario: The approved service-hour population is missing or unapproved.
counterexamples.reason: Do not allocate with a plug or silently substitute headcount; preserve the missing input and route for human review.

counterexamples.scenario: An agent uses the retained IAS 2 overview as US GAAP authority for the private manufacturer.
counterexamples.reason: IAS 2 is international context with local adoption and licensed-text limits; it is not silently reused as US authority.

counterexamples.scenario: An agent adds the $10,000 price effect at budget volume to the declared $9,000 sequential price effect.
counterexamples.reason: The two price effects use different conventions and double count the revenue bridge.

procedures: Identify the entity role, framework, period, and population.
Freeze and hash the source population and versions.
Tie the support pool to GL lines and exclude direct or one-off costs.
Calculate the primary allocation and independent sensitivity.
Calculate the declared sequential bridge and reject alternate double-counted components.
Reconcile entity profit to cash through AR, AP, and noncash items.
Keep restated actuals separate and preserve prior versions.
Escalate external applicability, missing drivers, and qualitative materiality to the responsible human.
evidence_controls: source record IDs and exact locators
GL account and driver join keys
deterministic_checks: restated actual replaces actual v1 and is not additive
data.expected_artifact: Versioned allocation schedule, driver sensitivity, budget-to-actual bridge, forecast/restate lineage, margin dictionary, profit-to-cash reconciliation, and external-applicability exception log.

examples.title: Complete synthetic allocation and bridge
examples.objective: Reproduce the primary allocation, sensitivity, sequential bridge, margin definitions, and cash tie from complete inputs.

examples.title: Missing approved driver
examples.objective: Stop rather than allocate from an unapproved substitute or plug.

mutations: Remove the approved service-hour log

examples.title: Independent headcount sensitivity
examples.objective: Preserve 30/70 headcount results as a sensitivity rather than a conclusion.

mutations: Run headcount allocation independently from service-hour allocation

examples.title: Restated actual after late invoice
examples.objective: Replace actual v1 with v2 while preserving lineage and avoiding additive double counting.

mutations: Add the $1,000 late January invoice to AP and restate direct cost

examples.title: Double-counted price bridge
examples.objective: Reject price at budget volume when the declared convention uses actual volume.

mutations: Add 1000 * (110 - 100) to the sequential price effect

examples.title: Internal allocation proposed for a federal award
examples.objective: Require external rule, award, and contract applicability review.

mutations: Apply the headcount sensitivity to a federal award without benefit or award documentation

limitations: All amounts and events are Original Synthetic project-created values; no customer, federal-award, federal-contract, or production records are included.
A reconciled synthetic model is not a professional opinion, operating-effectiveness test, forecast-accuracy study, or evidence that a driver is economically correct.
External source text is not stored and source rights remain record-specific and unresolved where not expressly granted.
No action, posting, payment, filing, certification, communication, or issue closure is authorized by this example.
